The British armies, which began the year holding the longest line in France and short of men, have ended it advancing on a broad front, with a large share of the prisoners and guns taken since August to their credit. The army that landed in August 1914 has been replaced several times over, and the Cabinet that sent it has been replaced twice. The argument between the generals and the politicians is not over, and will be carried on in print for the next twenty years.The front · 11 November 1918Expand the mapParisSaint-OmerMontreuilCalaisDoullensLondon-8MANPOWER ▾-3MUNITIONS ▾-3POLITICAL CAPITAL ▾Settled recordLanding, August 1914: assembled at Maubeuge.
